question: Do the exact NEON rotation pairs and the direct-interior pyrDown speed up the stable core's fixed-scale match, with bit-identical outputs?

before.source: git archive of 51d95b1 (UDOT dot product, frozen copy)

after.warp: NEON float64x2 pairs mirroring the fused scalar expressions; scalar warpPixel for edge pairs
after.pyrDown: direct interior columns, reflected edges, row pointers

toolchain: Apple clang 21.0.0, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, FPM_WITH_OPENCV=ON, default target-cpu apple-m1 for both builds
benchmark_modes: cpp-core/tools/benchmark_modes.py --repeats 9 (one warm-up + 9 measured per mode, fresh process each); sessions interleaved before,after x3; the before sessions run the frozen base copy of the script
control: legacy_cpp mode is the same macos-cli/match_core.cpp binary in both builds
fixture_ab: cpp-core/tools/benchmark_backend_ab.py --rounds 8 (round 0 warm-up discarded), alternating order, 17 compare_versions cases
metric: fpm_cli match_ms (excludes image decoding and learning); no runs dropped or rerun
acceptance: speed is reported, not gated; identity is gated separately (check_backend_identity.py 544 runs, compare_versions.py, core_test exact-reference test)
profiling: sample-based profiles are separate runs and are not formal timings
environment_note: other Claude sessions may be active on this machine; load averages are recorded per session
